Sauna Before Bed

There is little direct research on sauna and sleep. The closest evidence is a 2019 meta-analysis of warm baths and showers: heating the body 1 to 2 hours before bed improved self-rated sleep quality and sleep efficiency and helped people fall asleep about 10 minutes faster. If you try an evening sauna, finish at least an hour before bed, cool down, and drink water.
